title: Work, Power & Energy

notes.heading: 1. Work by Variable Forces, Work-Energy Theorem & Momentum-KE Link
notes.proseLatex: Work done by a general force along a path is $W = \int \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}$ (for constant force, $FD\cos\theta$; centripetal force does ZERO work since $\vec{F}_c \perp d\vec{r}$). The Work-Energy Theorem $W_{\text{all}} = W_{\text{cons}} + W_{\text{non-cons}} = \Delta K$ holds universally even with friction! Kinetic energy and momentum obey $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$, so for two bodies of equal momentum, the lighter body carries greater kinetic energy ($K \propto 1/m$).

keyFormulas.label: Work-Energy Theorem & Momentum-KE Relation
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Relate net work to kinetic-energy change and compare KE/momentum changes.

examples.problemLatex: If linear momentum of a rigid particle increases by $50\%$, by what percentage does its kinetic energy increase?
stepsLatex: From $K \propto p^2$, $p' = 1.5\,p \implies K' = (1.5)^2 K = 2.25\,K$ (do NOT use the small-error linear approximation $2\times 50\%$!).

notes.heading: 2. Conservative Forces, Spring Potential & Instantaneous Power
notes.proseLatex: Conservative forces ($\vec{F} = -\nabla U$, closed-loop work $\oint \vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r} = 0$) include gravity ($U = mgh$), electrostatics, and Hookean springs ($U_s = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$), conserving mechanical energy $E = K + U$ when $W_{\text{nc}} = 0$. Instantaneous power is $P = \frac{dW}{dt} = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}$; a vehicle driven by a constant-power engine ($Fv = P_0$) accelerates as $v\,dv/dx = P_0/(mv)$, giving $v \propto t^{1/2}$ and $x \propto t^{3/2}$.

keyFormulas.label: Potential Gradient, Spring Energy & Instantaneous Power
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Find equilibrium points (dU/dx = 0) and instantaneous power F.v.

notes.heading: 3. Vertical Circle Minimum Speeds & 1D Collisions
notes.proseLatex: To complete a vertical loop of radius $R$ attached to a light STRING, critical speeds are $v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{gR}$ and $v_{\text{bottom}} = \sqrt{5gR}$ (for a light rigid ROD, only $v_{\text{bottom}} = \sqrt{4gR}$ is needed since a rod supports compression at the top). In 1D collisions, coefficient of restitution $e = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2}$ satisfies $e=1$ (elastic: identical masses simply swap velocities!), $0<e<1$ (inelastic), and $e=0$ (perfectly inelastic coalescence).

keyFormulas.label: Vertical Loop Critical Speed & Coefficient of Restitution
keyFormulas.latex: $v_{\text{bot, string}} = \sqrt{5gR},\quad v_{\text{top, string}} = \sqrt{gR},\quad e = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2},\quad h_n = e^{2n}h_0$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Solve vertical loop critical speeds and bouncing-ball / 1D collision problems.

examples.problemLatex: A ball dropped from $h_0 = 16\text{ m}$ onto a floor with $e = 0.5$ rebounds twice. Find the height after the second bounce.
stepsLatex: After each bounce $v_{\text{up}} = e\,v_{\text{down}}$, so $h_n = e^{2n} h_0$.

wbjeebTraps: For finite changes ($\ge 5\%$) in $p$ or $v$, ALWAYS compute exact $(1 + \delta)^2 - 1$, never linear $2\delta$ (e.g., $+100\%$ in $p \implies +300\%$ in $K$, NOT $+200\%$!).
Linear momentum is conserved in ALL isolated collisions (elastic OR inelastic), whereas kinetic energy is conserved ONLY when $e = 1$.
Constant power $P_0$ does NOT give constant acceleration: $a = \frac{P_0}{mv}$ decreases as $v$ grows.

conceptPrimer.heading: Work by Variable Forces & the Zero-Work Cases
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $W = \int\vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}$ (constant force: $FD\cos\theta$). Centripetal force does ZERO work ($\vec{F}\perp d\vec{r}$ always). Micro-check: $F = 10\,\text{N}$ at $60°$ over $5\,\text{m}$: $W = 25\,\text{J}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Work-Energy Theorem & the $K$-$p$ Link
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $W_{\text{all}} = \Delta K$ holds universally, friction included. $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$: equal momenta $\Rightarrow$ the LIGHTER body carries more $K$ ($K \propto 1/m$); equal speeds $\Rightarrow$ $K \propto m$. Micro-check: $m$ vs $2m$ at equal $p$: $K$ ratio $2 : 1$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Conservative Forces & Spring Energy
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Conservative $\oint\vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r} = 0$, $\vec{F} = -\nabla U$: gravity $U = mgh$, spring $U_s = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$. With $W_{\text{nc}} = 0$, $E = K + U$ is conserved. Micro-check: $k = 500$, $x = 0.2$: $U_s = 10\,\text{J}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Percent Changes: Exact, Not Linear
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$: small changes allow $\frac{\Delta K}{K} \approx 2\frac{\Delta p}{p}$, but finite ones need $(1+\delta)^2 - 1$: $+100\%$ in $p$ gives $4K - K = +300\%$, NOT $+200\%$. Micro-check: $\delta = 0.1$: $21\%$, slightly more than linear $20\%$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Constant-Power Vehicles
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $P_0 = Fv = mv\frac{dv}{dt}$ gives $v \propto t^{1/2}$ and $x \propto t^{3/2}$, with $a = \frac{P_0}{mv}$ decreasing as $v$ grows. Micro-check: $m = 1000\,\text{kg}$, $P_0 = 50\,\text{kW}$, $v = 10$: $a = 5\,\text{m/s}^2$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Vertical Circle Minimum Speeds & Collision Restitution
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: String loop radius $R$: $v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{gR}$, $v_{\text{bottom}} = \sqrt{5gR}$; a rigid ROD needs only $v_{\text{bottom}} = \sqrt{4gR}$. Restitution $e = \frac{v_2 - v_1}{u_1 - u_2}$: $e = 1$ elastic (equal masses swap velocities), $0 < e < 1$ inelastic, $e = 0$ coalescence. Momentum is conserved in ALL collisions. Micro-check: $e = 1$, equal masses, $u_1 = 6$, $u_2 = 0$: $v_1 = 0$, $v_2 = 6$.

Closed-loop work zero; defines potential energy.

memoryHooks: Momentum always conserved; KE only if elastic.
commonMistakes: Using linear $2\delta$ for percent changes beyond $\sim 5\%$.
Dropping the $\frac{1}{2}$ in spring or stored-work energy.
Claiming KE is conserved in inelastic collisions.
Writing $P = Fv$ without the angle in the dot product.
Forgetting $W_{\text{nc}}$ terms in the work-energy theorem.
Mixing up string and rod loop speeds.
Rushing the final unit conversion after a correct setup.
examChecklist: Use exact $(1+\delta)^2 - 1$ for finite percent changes.
Vertical-circle minimum speeds: string vs rod.
